absent: Locking and concurrency rules for control-area access and cached guest mappings.
Full data layouts of control areas, segment descriptors, bitmaps and host-mapping structures.
Host-state and entry/exit-control subchecks beyond the execution-control fragment shown.
State-machine transitions for timers, posted interrupts and enlightened clean fields.
Complete error-code and failure-code contract for nested entry validation.

findings.text: Real-mode segment acceptance normalizes privilege to the most privileged level and normalizes code type to a fixed readable accessed value, then requires paragraph-scaled base equality, full 16-bit limit, and one fixed encoded rights value.

Protected code acceptance requires usable and present descriptor with system flag and code plus accessed type attributes; writable code permits descriptor privilege at or above requestor privilege, while non-writable code requires descriptor privilege equal to requestor privilege.

Stack acceptance treats unusable as valid and otherwise allows two data type encodings with system flag, privilege equality and present set. Data acceptance treats unusable as valid and otherwise requires system flag and present, with descriptor privilege not below requestor privilege for the more constrained type family.

Task register must be usable with table-indicator clear, one of two system types, and present set. Local descriptor table may be unusable; otherwise it needs table-indicator clear, a dedicated system type and present set. Code and stack requestor privilege fields must agree.

Nested guest control-register state is accepted only under fixed zero/one masks, with protection and paging mask bits relaxed under unrestricted guest. Paging without protection, CET without write protect, and 64-bit entry without address extensions and paging are rejected; pending EFER load additionally requires EFER validity and mode-bit coherence.

Debug, pattern-table, performance, bound-config and CET guest fields are examined only when the matching entry-load control is enabled. The debug path supports a compatibility quirk for a management-freeze bit, and CET validation covers control value validity, stack-pointer alignment and table address form including extended canonicality.

An invalid link-pointer sentinel passes without further work. Any other link value needs a valid guest address, successful cached guest read, expected nested revision, and shadow indicator matching host capability. Non-register activity is limited to active, halted and wait-for-startup states.

Pin, primary and conditional secondary execution controls must satisfy allowed-mask rules. Further gates include target-count limit, I/O, MSR, shadow, APIC, NMI, logging, unrestricted, mode-EPT and shadow subcontrols, non-zero virtual-processor identifier when enabled, timer-save implying timer, EPT pointer validity, function mask and list validity, and non-zero time-scale factor.

Nested page setup reloads PAE tables when needed, then maps APIC-access, virtual-APIC and posted-interrupt pages from guest addresses into host pointers. Missing backing fails setup, clears posted-interrupt enable with a null descriptor, and either clears unused shadow or programs an illegal address to force later entry failure; MSR-bitmap use follows preparation outcome.

MSR-bitmap preparation is skipped without hardware or guest enable, or under an enlightened no-change indication. Otherwise the guest bitmap is mapped read-only, the host bitmap is seeded to intercept the extended-APIC window, selectively relaxed for priority and optionally completion and self-IPI under virtualized modes, and merged with host policy for segment, speculation, frequency, CET, supervisor-stack and counter families.
Restored nested-state validation is externally visible and succeeds only when optional shadow-header checks plus execution, host-state and guest-state control checks all succeed.

Some malformed nested page configurations do not fail immediately with guest-visible semantics but program an illegal host pointer or defer handling, so callers must treat setup success as provisional until entry is attempted.
The extended-APIC MSR window covers 256 consecutive selectors beginning at 2048, maintained as separate read and write halves indexed in machine-word units.
Nested link validation uses a fixed invalid-address sentinel for absence, a fixed expected revision for header match, and a fixed control-area size for cached guest access.
